opening_message:
Ticket 1: Casey Wu (employee ID E005) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E005.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Casey Wu (E005) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted; write is the maximum for this employee. Requested write is within policy, recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Casey Wu (E005) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, the maximum is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommending read.
reason: The two notes for Casey Wu (E005) conflict: one says full-time Payroll Specialist (max write for Source Code), while the other says contractor with basic security training (max read for Source Code). Because the evidence is contradictory, I cannot establish that write is within policy. Granting read is the safest level that is within policy under both interpretations (full-time allows read; contractor with basic training allows read).
